reason: E1 shows a CrTaO4-based oxide layer formed and was protective at 1100 °C, supporting the first premise, but it does not vary Ta content, so the specific claims about Ta content driving CrTaO4 formation, diffusion control, and outperforming other oxides are not directly supported by the cited evidence. E2 even notes that CrTaO4 may hinder protective Al2O3 or Cr2O3, which partially contradicts the premise that it outweighs competing oxides.
premises: CrTaO4-based oxide layers can be continuous and protective in refractory HEAs
Sufficient Ta promotes formation of a dense CrTaO4-based oxide layer
CrTaO4 layer limits outward cation diffusion and inward oxygen diffusion
Higher Ta content leads to lower weight gain and more uniform CrTaO4-dominated oxide
